answer: Each identity posts a registration bond fully slashed on proven double-claiming, so an attacker farming many wallets posts it per account and forfeits all of it when one copy is caught. A shared nullifier enforces single personhood: an extra account presenting the same oasis is rejected before claiming any reward. Cheap identity multiplication thus becomes a stack of fully collateralised bets; once slash probability beats the bond-to-reward ratio, expected return turns negative, so a terrace of hundreds of accounts only strands capital. A slow spiral of rate limits raises cost.
